title: Kruskal's minimum spanning tree
summary: Sort all edges by weight and take each one that does not close a cycle. A union-find array tracks the groups.

checkpoints.text: The six edges are copied into three arrays: one end, the other end, the weight.
The edges are sorted by weight, cheapest first. `parent` gives every vertex its own group: each one is its own leader.
The cheapest edge, 0 – 2 (weight 1), joins two different groups, so it is taken. Group 0 now points at group 2.
Edge 0 – 1 (weight 4): `find` follows `parent` from 0 and from 1 to the same leader, so 0 and 1 are already connected. Taking this edge would close a cycle, so it is skipped.
The same tree as Prim, total weight 11, found a different way. Sorting the edges dominates: O(E log E) with a fast sort.
